newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's airline purchase new B.737-500 airplane.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's airline purchase new B.737-500 airplane.

text.p: Morocco's airline Royal Air Maroc (RAM) purchased a new Boeing 737-500 plane as a part of its ongoing programme to reinforce its fleet, a spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
"The acquisition of this new airplane aims to renew and modernise RAM's medium distance fleet," a Moroccan national carrier spokeswoman told Reuters.
The purchase which was effective on March 1, 1997, followed the company decision "to withdraw B.727-200 airplanes from the service next year", the spokeswoman said but gave no details.
RAM did not disclose the price of the new airplane.
The state-run Royal Air Maroc is expected to purchase two B.737-800 in 1998, she said. Average age of its medium distance fleet "will not exceed seven years," RAM added.

Royal Air Maroc at present operates 27 aircrafts, mainly Boeings, and made a net profit of 74 million dirahams ($7.8 million) in the first eight months of 1996, carrying 1.8 million passengers, according to latest available figures.
